LESSON: LIGHT

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: FORCE AND ENERGY
Topic 3.1: Light

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Light. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does light travel?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate the movement of light through materials
2. draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors
3. describe the formation of rainbow in nature
4. appreciate the importance of movement light in everyday life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LIGHT
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Light helps you succeed in SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: LIGHT
Light is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Demonstrate the movement of light through materials

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate the movement of light through materials. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate the movement of light through materials.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Light” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate the movement of light through materials. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors

What this means
In this part you learn to draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Light matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe the formation of rainbow in nature

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the formation of rainbow in nature. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the formation of rainbow in nature.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Light this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the formation of rainbow in nature. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of movement light in everyday life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of movement light in everyday life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of movement light in everyday life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Light” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of movement light in everyday life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Light is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Light” around your school. (skill: demonstrate the movement of light through materials)

Example 2: Say why Light matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Light this week. (skill: describe the formation of rainbow in nature)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Light” around your school. (skill: appreciate the importance of movement light in everyday life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Light to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate the movement of light through materials.
3. Practise this skill: draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors.
4. Practise this skill: describe the formation of rainbow in nature.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Light from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Light: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Light?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does light travel?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Light means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate the movement of light through materials.
5. Be able to: draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
